text: VARDEN, July 14 — The new Isolde-class ferry is designed to carry 1,800 passengers and 420 vehicles, according to people familiar with the matter. The first vessel, slated for service next spring on the Rellan Strait route, is undergoing final interior fit-out at North Quay Shipworks, where workers installed the main lounges and evacuation systems this week. People familiar with the matter said the operator, Seabridge Line, plans a two-week trial in August before taking delivery in October. The ferries will use dual-fuel engines and feature expanded children’s areas, a small clinic and upgraded accessibility lifts, part of a fleet renewal program announced last year.
